A1.justification: Both PDFs describe S4D and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Content can be matched despite section moves, renumbering, and v1's duplicated bibliography.

before.justification: V1 reports original reconstruction results on Neu3DV and CMU-Panoptic in Tables 1–2, alongside control-point and optical-flow ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments in Tables 2–3 and the main text and appendices, and adds training-time comparisons in Table 1.

M1.justification: The four-module pipeline, optical-flow motion decoupling, control-point interpolation, keyframe residual compensation, and loss are retained. V2's reordered exposition and quaternion-normalization clarification do not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same six Neu3DV sequences and three CMU-Panoptic sequences for multiview dynamic reconstruction, including the longer flame_salmon_1 sequence. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Dynamic-GS and 4D-GS retain their corresponding quantitative and qualitative comparisons. The PWC, SpyNet, and DIS comparison also remains. V2 mentions 3DGStream only in related work; it is not an added evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The stated 4D-GS training-budget expansion for flame_salmon_1 changes from 30k to 120k iterations in v1 Section 4.1 to 17k to 68k in v2 Appendix .5. This is a reported setting revision; unchanged corresponding scores do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Initial-scene quality correlations, pruning, no/partial/full-control ablations, optical-flow comparisons, motion visualizations, and supplementary qualitative examples are retained. Pruning and optical-flow analyses move into the appendix without new experimental evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V2's dataset-average scores do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V2 Table 1 adds average reconstruction metrics and training times: 57.35 hours for Dynamic-GS, 6.88 for 4D-GS, and 12.19/3.94/1.89 for GoS1/5/10. GoS10 flame_steak LPIPS changes from 0.7330 to 0.0733; other per-scene values remain unchanged. The new GoS10 average PSNR of 30.91 slightly differs from the approximately 30.90 mean of Table 2.

T1.justification: The motion-projection equations, interpolation formulation, GoS representation, and Appendix .1 near-parallel-ray proof are retained. Equation renumbering, explicit coordinate notation, and explanatory clarifications do not introduce substantive mathematical changes.

C1.justification: Both retain the contributions of partially learned discrete 6-DoF control points and a streaming Gaussian reconstruction pipeline, with the same accuracy and fast-optimization claims. The abstract's added 100-iteration detail was already reported in v1 Section 4.1.

C2.justification: V1 explains that SAM-track fails when objects enter or leave views, causing CMU-Panoptic motion manipulation to operate on the entire foreground instead of individual objects. V2 retains mask reuse but omits this qualification. Initial-reconstruction dependence and lack of monocular support remain stated.

D1.justification: V2 omits v1's explicit PyTorch implementation, Adam beta values of (0.9, 0.999), three-nearest-control-point choice, and Neu3DV one-camera test split. It adds clarification about quaternion normalization omitted from the displayed formula. These documentation differences do not establish changes to the underlying implementation.

R1.justification: V2 adds a brief discussion of 3DGStream's Neural Transformation Cache in Section 2.1 and removes the Adam and PyTorch references. The broader positioning relative to NeRF, Gaussian reconstruction, and sparse control points remains stable.

P1.justification: The main text is extensively rewritten across the abstract, introduction, related work, methodology, and experiments. Method subsections are reordered to follow the pipeline, several discussions move to the appendix, and the duplicated bibliography is removed.

P2.justification: V2 adds a compact average-results and timing table, relocates pruning and optical-flow displays to the appendix, and revises captions, labels, headers, and styling. Existing diagrams, plots, and qualitative image panels retain their substantive visual content.

improvement.justification: The added timing comparison, corrected LPIPS entry, clearer workflow organization, and removal of duplicated references make v2 easier to assess. These limited gains are partly offset by omitted implementation and segmentation-failure details and the small inconsistency between the new average PSNR and the per-scene table.
